units.translation: 52. ἠθεῖαι: a form of address in Homer from younger to older persons. Apollonius, however, has used a collective expression; for he has applied what belongs to Hera also to Athena. These things will be fitting to say according to the poetry of Homer. But according to the younger poets, she is older not only than Athena and Hera, but also than Zeus; for Hesiod (Theog. 188 ff.) says that she was born from the genitals of Uranus.

62. λυόμενος χαλκέων: he has taken Ixion, because he is thought to have attempted violence against Hera. Ixion was the son of Phlegyas, as also Euripides (fg 424 N.²): 'Son of Phlegyas, lord Ixion'. Pherecydes (3 fg 51 b J.) however 〈...〉 of Antion. They say that after marrying Dia, daughter of Eioneus, he promised to give many gifts. When Eioneus came for these, he made a pit, heated it, and covered it with thin wood and fine dust; Eioneus fell in and perished. Madness fell upon Ixion because of this, and no one was willing to purify him, neither gods nor men; for he was the first to kill a kinsman. Zeus took pity on him and purified him. After being purified, he fell in love with Hera; Zeus made a cloud resembling Hera and laid it beside him, and later made a four-spoked wheel, bound him to it, and punished him.
